title: Flash-Sale Batch Processor Microtask Queue Starvation
businessContext: During Black Friday peak traffic on a flash-sale e-commerce platform, the checkout order-ingestion service experiences severe WebSocket heartbeat timeouts and dropping health-check endpoints, leading Kubernetes to repeatedly restart healthy pods.
problemStatement: The order batching function processes order queues recursively using Promise.resolve().then(processNextOrder). While CPU load appears moderate (~65%), the HTTP server stops responding to TCP health probes and WebSocket ping/pongs disconnect thousands of shoppers. Diagnose why the event loop is blocked and implement a cooperative scheduling mechanism.
constraints: Orders must continue to process with maximum throughput without starving macrotasks (I/O, timers, incoming network packets).
Memory consumption must remain bounded under a 50,000 order surge.
candidateTasks: Identify why Promise.resolve().then() recursion starves macrotasks like I/O and setTimeout.
Refactor the processor to use cooperative scheduling (e.g., yielding via setImmediate or setTimeout every N iterations or when a budget threshold is exceeded).
Explain the difference in event loop phases (Timer, Poll, Check, Microtask drain).
hints: Microtasks (Promise reactions, queueMicrotask, process.nextTick) are drained completely before the event loop advances to the next macrotask phase.
If microtasks continually queue more microtasks, macrotasks (such as socket I/O, HTTP server accept, ping/pong timers) never get executed.
Introduce a batch threshold (e.g. process 50 items) or a time slice budget (e.g. 8ms), then yield control using setImmediate() or setTimeout(..., 0).

testCases.name: Processes small batch accurately
testCases.explanation: Small batches should resolve successfully without unbounded delay.

testCases.name: Yields cooperatively on large batch
testCases.explanation: Large orders must complete without starving macrotasks.

alternativeApproaches: Using Async Generators with for-await-of loop and time-budgeted yields.
Offloading heavy batch ingestion to Node.js Worker Threads (worker_threads) with SharedArrayBuffer or message passing.
commonMistakes: Replacing Promise.resolve().then() with setImmediate on every single item, introducing 100x timer bookkeeping overhead.
Converting to a synchronous while loop, which freezes the event loop completely for seconds.
Using process.nextTick(), which is even more aggressive than Promises and immediately crashes process health checks.
